item.title: [LU-19536] fault_in_iov_iter_readable() with a spinlock held
item.description:
in LU-13805 and LU-18006 the following code was introduced:

       if (rw == WRITE) {
               spin_lock(&sdio->csd_lock);
...
       /* fault in the entire userspace iovec */
       if (rw == WRITE) {
               if (unlikely(ll_iov_iter_fault_in_readable(iter, count)))

I think it's a bad idea to repopulate userspace pages holding a spinlock - this can involve page allocation and I/O.

status.description: This issue was once resolved, but the resolution was deemed incorrect. From here issues are either marked assigned or resolved.

sanity test_398v fails with ENOSPC when it runs late in a full sanity run on small (400MB) OSTs, and passes when run alone:

dd: error writing '/mnt/lustre/f398v.sanity': No space left on device
 sanity test_398v: @@@@@@ FAIL: DIO write failed

There are two causes:

  1. By then the client holds nearly all free space on OST0000 as grant, e.g. 240869376 bytes of grant with kbytesavail=236192 (241860608 bytes) and tot_granted=242186688. The DIO extents that fall back to unaccounted RPCs at the max_dirty_mb limit need ungranted space on the OST, so tgt_grant_check() refuses them with ENOSPC, although the same client holds over 200MB of unused grant. This happens with no grant mismatch at all: the test printed grant before DIO: client=243015680 server=243015680 delta=0. Either test_398v needs to release the excess grant before the DIO (e.g. by lowering osc.*.cur_grant_bytes), or the OST should let unaccounted DIO pages of a client use that client's own unused grant.
  2. The OST also leaks grant for writes refused before tgt_grant_prepare_write(). The client counts the grant of such a write as used. Its resend after a recoverable error has OBD_FL_RECOV_RESEND, so tgt_grant_check() skips the grant ("Recoverable resend arrived, skipping accounting"), and a write refused with a non-recoverable error is never charged at all. After the fail_loc tests of sanity 118 (118j OBD_FAIL_OST_BRW_WRITE_BULK2, 118k OBD_FAIL_OST_BRW_WRITE_BULK) the OST counts about 10MB more grant for the client than the client has, until it reconnects, which makes (1) more likely.

A patch for (2) with a new sanity test_64k will follow under this ticket, based on patch https://review.whamcloud.com/69572 ("LU-20727 target: don't dealloc grant the export no longer has"). It fixes the refused-write leak, but about 5MB of drift from 118k remains and is still being investigated. It does not address (1).
